Subject: Implementation: SSO/SCIM/IP allowlist & Service Account Ownership — First 30 days

Hi Samantha — great to meet you during last week's exec call. I wanted to kick off the implementation plan specifically for identity and network controls so we have clarity on responsibilities and an achievable 30-day runbook for TerraNova's rollout to production.

Attached: terranova-sso-scim-ip-template.xlsx (a two-tab workbook: SSO/SCIM details + IP ranges/service-account owners) and a one-page kickoff agenda (redwood-kickoff-agenda.pdf).

High-level asks today (can you reply inline?):
- Confirm SSO provider and whether SAML metadata is available for our test tenant (Okta, Ping, etc.). If you have an XML file, please attach.
- Confirm SCIM provisioning status and whether you want redwood to push users or to consume a SCIM endpoint.
- Confirm IP allowlist ranges for both staging and production (CIDR entries).
- Identify a single owner for service account provisioning and a backup (name + email).

Proposed responsibilities (we can adjust):
- Redwood: SAML config verification, SCIM provisioning guidance, temporary staging allowlist, runbook for service account lifecycle.
- TerraNova: Provide SAML metadata, approve IP ranges, designate SA owners, and test accounts for SCIM sync.

Next steps:
1) Please fill the attached workbook where you can and return by EOD Tuesday.
2) We'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive (engineering + infra) — suggested windows are Thu 9/30 10–12 PT or Fri 10/1 1–3 PT.

Thanks — want to make this low-friction so you can hit production gating on schedule.

-Jordan

Jordan — adding a quick operational note and a draft ownership matrix so TerraNova can see who touches what. I'm happy to run the deep-dive and own the SCIM checklist. Ben, can you own service-account provisioning and create the RBAC template we discussed?

Draft ownership matrix (first 30 days):
- SAML config & smoke test: Jordan Blake (redwood) — jordan.blake@redwood.com
- SCIM sync setup & initial sync: Monica Patel (redwood) — monica.patel@redwood.com
- Service account provisioning & naming conventions: Ben Carter (redwood) — ben.carter@redwood.com
- TerraNova SA owner: TBD (TerraNova)
- IP allowlist approval: TerraNova Network Ops (rdops@terranova.com)

A couple of internal constraints to flag:
- For staged testing we prefer a max of 3 CIDR blocks to avoid firewall churn. If TerraNova needs a wider range for endpoint testing, we can use a time-boxed temporary exception with an explicit rollback after validation.
- Service accounts should follow the naming prefix tn-svc- and include an expiration tag in the metadata for automatic re-certification.

I'll attach a lightweight checklist in the shared drive and will populate the SCIM run steps after the deep-dive.

-Monica

Thanks Jordan and Monica — this looks good. Quick answers inline: 
- SSO: Okta (we'll export SAML metadata) — attached terranova-saml-metadata.xml.
- SCIM: We have SCIM enabled on our Okta org and can give an API token for provisioning. We prefer Redwood to push users to a "redwood-staging" group first.
- IP ranges: Staging: 54.213.128.0/22, 34.201.64.0/24. Production: 54.213.120.0/22. Please note these are our perimeter egress ranges and are subject to change — rdops@terranova.com is cc'd to confirm.
- Service account owner: Assign initial owner to myself (samantha.lee@terranova.com) and backup is Nathan Park <nathan.park@terranova.com>. We like the suggested tn-svc- prefix.

Regarding timeline: we can target SCIM initial sync and SAML smoke test in the staging environment by 10/7, and production cutover the week of 10/13 pending smoke results. Is that feasible for Redwood?

One ask from security: do you have a standard SAML attribute map for email, name, and employee_id? If you can share that ahead of the deep-dive, we'll pre-map in Okta.

Samantha Lee
